<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="ניסן_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918187_theRebbe_312" batchId="meluket-_D7_A0_D7_99_D7_A1_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918187_theRebbe_312__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that there are two modes of divine conduct: natural (associated with Tishrei) and miraculous (associated with Nissan), and that the redemption began on Rosh Chodesh Nissan.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">However, the concept is,</t>
    <t s="2">based on what is said in the Akeidah,</t>
    <t s="3">that in the conduct of the world by the Holy One, blessed be He, there are two modes.</t>
    <t s="4">Natural conduct,</t>
    <t s="5">and conduct that is above nature, which is miraculous conduct.</t>
    <t s="6">And this is the difference between Rosh Hashanah, which is on the first of Tishrei, and Rosh Chodesh Nissan,</t>
    <t s="7">for the first of Tishrei is the New Year for natural conduct,</t>
    <t s="8">and in the language of the verse, "the statutes of heaven and earth."</t>
    <t s="9">And regarding this it is said, "seed and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter... shall not cease,"</t>
    <t s="10">which includes all the changes throughout the months of the year,</t>
    <t s="11">and as it is brought in the Gemara,</t>
    <t s="12">"Half of Tishrei, Marcheshvan, and half of Kislev are for sowing, etc.,"</t>
    <t s="13">meaning,</t>
    <t s="14">that each of these six seasons includes two months of the year.</t>
    <t s="15">And Rosh Chodesh Nissan is the New Year for miraculous conduct,</t>
    <t s="16">which is the matter of the redemption of the Exodus from Egypt, which occurred in the month of Nissan in a miraculous manner.</t>
    <t s="17">And the beginning of the redemption was on Rosh Chodesh Nissan,</t>
    <t s="18">when the section of "This month is for you" was said, in which the commandment of the Paschal sacrifice was also stated,</t>
    <t s="19">as it is brought in the Mechilta</t>
    <t s="20">(cited in Rashi)</t>
    <t s="21">on the verse,</t>
    <t s="22">"And they went and did,"</t>
    <t s="23">"But had they already done [it]?</t>
    <t s="24">Rather, once they accepted upon themselves to do [it], Scripture credits them as if they had done [it]."</t>
    <t s="25">And it is also hinted at in the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory,</t>
    <t s="26">"One might think from Rosh Chodesh, etc."</t>
    <t s="27">[And particularly according to the interpretation</t>
    <t s="28">"One might think from Rosh Chodesh"</t>
    <t s="29">(not merely as a possibility to be rejected,</t>
    <t s="30">but rather)</t>
    <t s="31">as a settled conclusion,</t>
    <t s="32">that it could already be from Rosh Chodesh,</t>
    <t s="33">except that it is not comparable to how it is on that day,</t>
    <t s="34">and particularly at the time when matzah and maror are placed before you],</t>
    <t s="35">from which it is understood that the matter of the redemption began already from Rosh Chodesh Nissan,</t>
    <t s="36">which is the New Year for miraculous conduct.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that natural conduct is constant and set by G-d for the world, while miraculous conduct is a renewal connected to Yaakov's children, drawn down specifically through their own service.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, the difference between natural conduct</t>
    <t s="2">(Tishrei)</t>
    <t s="3">and miraculous conduct</t>
    <t s="4">(Nissan),</t>
    <t s="5">is understood based on the saying of our Rabbis, of blessed memory,</t>
    <t s="6">"When the Holy One, blessed be He, chose His world, He established for it new moons and years,</t>
    <t s="7">and when He chose Yaakov and his sons, He established for them a new moon of redemption,"</t>
    <t s="8">meaning,</t>
    <t s="9">that natural conduct is the conduct that the Holy One, blessed be He, established in His world to be continuous without interruption,</t>
    <t s="10">in contrast, miraculous conduct, which is in a manner of renewal, is connected with Yaakov and his sons,</t>
    <t s="11">for its drawing down is specifically through the service of Israel with their own power.</t>
    <t s="12">And as is emphasized in the Exodus from Egypt, which was in the merit of the blood of the Paschal sacrifice and the blood of circumcision,</t>
    <t s="13">and as it is written,</t>
    <t s="14">"And I said to you, 'In your blood, live,' and I said to you, 'In your blood, live'... and you were naked and bare..."</t>
    <t s="15">And this matter began already on Rosh Chodesh,</t>
    <t s="16">as mentioned above,</t>
    <t s="17">for then they accepted to fulfill the commandment, "They shall take for themselves, each man a lamb, etc.,"</t>
    <t s="18">in which the strength in the service of the Children of Israel is emphasized,</t>
    <t s="19">that despite the lamb being the deity of Egypt,</t>
    <t s="20">the Children of Israel were not influenced by the Egyptians and took the lamb to slaughter it as a sacrifice to G-d,</t>
    <t s="21">which is a miraculous conduct in the matter of service</t>
    <t s="22">[And to add,</t>
    <t s="23">that in this matter there is a novelty on Rosh Chodesh Nissan and on the tenth of the month, even regarding the fifteenth of Nissan,</t>
    <t s="24">because on Rosh Chodesh Nissan they were still in the exile of Egypt,</t>
    <t s="25">and nevertheless they were not influenced by the Egyptians, etc.],</t>
    <t s="26">and through this they caused that there should also be conduct from Above in a miraculous manner.</t>
    <t s="27">And the concept in this is,</t>
    <t s="28">that specifically through service with one's own power,</t>
    <t s="29">they draw down a new influence that is above the influence that exists continuously,</t>
    <t s="30">because,</t>
    <t s="31">the influence that exists continuously is only from the aspect of externality,</t>
    <t s="32">and through service with one's own power, they draw down from the aspect of internality.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that miraculous conduct reveals a higher level than natural conduct, a level beyond the statement "I am G-d, I have not changed," which is above the framework of change entirely.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">And an explanation of the matter,</t>
    <t s="2">for, behold,</t>
    <t s="3">even though in natural conduct the greatness of the Creator is also evident,</t>
    <t s="4">and moreover, specifically in natural conduct in a manner of "they shall not cease," the concept of "I am G-d, I have not changed" is manifest and revealed,</t>
    <t s="5">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="6">in miraculous conduct, a more elevated level is revealed, which is above even the aspect of "I am G-d, I have not changed."</t>
    <t s="7">And the concept in this is,</t>
    <t s="8">that what is written "I am G-d, I have not changed" is in a level that has a connection and gives place to the matter of change,</t>
    <t s="9">therefore it is necessary to negate and say "I am G-d, I have not</t>
    <t s="10">changed,"</t>
    <t s="11">in contrast, in the level that is entirely above the category of change,</t>
    <t s="12">it is not applicable at all to say "I have not changed."</t>
    <t s="13">And in the language of our master, the Alter Rebbe, in Shaar HaYichud VeHaEmunah,</t>
    <t s="14">that if one were to say about some lofty and deep wisdom that it is impossible to touch it with hands because of the depth of the concept, behold, everyone who hears would laugh at him,</t>
    <t s="15">and this is because wisdom has no value or connection to the sense of touch,</t>
    <t s="16">and therefore it is not applicable to negate the matter of touch regarding it.</t>
    <t s="17">And similarly, it is not applicable to negate the matter of change in the level that is entirely above the matter of change.</t>
    <t s="18">And analogous to what is explained in the Responsa of the Rashba</t>
    <t s="19">(cited in Sefer HaChakirah of the Tzemach Tzedek)</t>
    <t s="20">in explaining the verse,</t>
    <t s="21">"And You are He, and Your years shall not end,"</t>
    <t s="22">that the verse speaks within the category of time</t>
    <t s="23">(which is within the comprehension of man, who is limited),</t>
    <t s="24">this is the matter of "Your years,"</t>
    <t s="25">and within the category of time there is a need to negate and say "shall not end,"</t>
    <t s="26">but it is not applicable to say this regarding the level that is entirely above time</t>
    <t s="27">[like the aspect of Shabbos, which is above time,</t>
    <t s="28">therefore on every Sunday we say "today is the first day of the week to Shabbos,"</t>
    <t s="29">even though many hundreds and thousands of days have passed since the creation of the world,</t>
    <t s="30">because the aspect of Shabbos is entirely above time.</t>
    <t s="31">And similarly regarding Rosh Chodesh, which is analogous to Shabbos].</t>
    <t s="32">And this is that natural conduct</t>
    <t s="33">(in which it is necessary to negate the matter of change,</t>
    <t s="34">"I am G-d, I have not changed")</t>
    <t s="35">is drawn from the aspect of externality,</t>
    <t s="36">in contrast, miraculous conduct</t>
    <t s="37">(in which it is not applicable to negate the matter of change)</t>
    <t s="38">is from the aspect of internality, which is entirely above worlds.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
